name: Pazhampathinathar Temple, Thiruppunavayil (Thiruppunavasal)
deity: Shiva as Pazhampathinathar (Vriddhapureeswarar), with the goddess Periyanayaki
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Pandya Nadu near the Palk Bay coast, sung by Sambandar (7th century) and Sundarar in the Tevaram
summary: Near the sea in Pudukkottai district, at the Thiruppunavayil of the Tevaram, Shiva is worshipped as Pazhampathinathar, the Lord of the ancient town, on one of the broadest lingam pedestals in the Tamil country.

sections.history: Thiruppunavasal is a village close to the Palk Bay coast in Pudukkottai district, some 25 km south of Avudaiyarkoil, and its temple is the Thiruppunavayil of the Tevaram. It is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and is counted seventh among the fourteen of Pandya Nadu. Both of its names for the Lord — the Tamil Pazhampathinathar and the Sanskrit Vriddhapureeswarar — mean the Lord of the ancient town, a sign of how old the shrine was felt to be. Sambandar sang here, probably on his way from Vedaranyam to Madurai, and Sundarar came later in the company of his friend, the Chera king Cheraman Perumal.
sections.architecture: A rajagopuram of about 65 feet marks the entrance, and the building is often described as blending Pandya and Chola manners. The lingam of the main sanctum rests on an exceptionally broad pedestal, said to be among the largest in circumference of any in the Tamil country. The goddess Periyanayaki has her own east-facing shrine. The enclosures hold shrines of the Pancha Vinayakas, Dakshinamurthy, Murugan with Valli and Deivanai, Brahma and Gajalakshmi, and the Pambar river runs just south of the temple.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Brahma, unable to explain the meaning of the sacred syllable Om, lost his power to create. On Parvati's counsel he came to this ancient place, installed a four-faced lingam and worshipped Shiva, until his creative office was restored. The temple also honours the nine sons of the sage Kapila, who have a shrine of their own among its enclosures.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festivals of the year: monthly Pradosham, Maha Shivaratri, Arudra Darshanam in Margazhi and the Navaratri days of the goddess Periyanayaki. Sung by both Sambandar and Sundarar, it is also a stop for pilgrims making the round of Pandya Nadu's Tevaram temples. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thiruppunavasal is a quiet coastal village, and the temple's tall gopuram rises above the low coastal country close to the sea. Stand before the great pedestal of the lingam, visit Periyanayaki in her own shrine, and pair the journey with Avudaiyarkoil, the famous temple of Manikkavasagar a short drive to the north.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples of the region. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruppunavasal lies in southern Pudukkottai district near the coast, about 25–30 km south of Avudaiyarkoil; buses connect it with Aranthangi and Pudukkottai. Aranthangi and Pudukkottai have the nearest railway stations, and Tiruchirappalli and Madurai airports are each a few hours away by road.
